title: Masque at 26, Naar at 49: Two Indian Restaurants Make World's 50 Best 2026
excerpt: Mumbai's Masque and Kasauli's 16-seat Naar both debuted on The World's 50 Best Restaurants 2026, topped by Spain's Asador Etxebarri. Naar also won the Sustainable Restaurant Award.
body:
• Two Indian restaurants debuted on The World's 50 Best Restaurants 2026: Masque in Mumbai at No. 26 and Naar in Kasauli, Himachal Pradesh, at No. 49.
  • Spain's Asador Etxebarri, in the Basque village of Axpe, topped the list, followed by Bangkok's Gaggan at No. 2 and Copenhagen's Alchemist at No. 3.
  • Naar, chef Prateek Sadhu's 16-seat Himalayan restaurant, also won the Sustainable Restaurant Award 2026.
  • The ranking is voted by The World's 50 Best Restaurants Academy, comprising over 1,000 independent food writers, chefs and culinary experts.

India has two new entries on the world's most watched restaurant ranking. Masque in Mumbai placed 26th and Naar in Kasauli placed 49th on The World's 50 Best Restaurants 2026, both as new entries, according to Lifestyle Asia's report of the full list. At the top, Spain's Asador Etxebarri claimed first place, celebrated for its fire-based cooking, with Bangkok's Gaggan at No. 2 and Copenhagen's Alchemist at No. 3, Robb Report India reported. Asia accounts for 15 restaurants on this year's list, with Bangkok alone contributing five.

Masque: Indian ingredients, reworked

Masque, set within a former textile mill in Mumbai's Mahalaxmi area, reinterprets indigenous ingredients and culinary traditions through seasonal menus and contemporary techniques. "At Masque, situated within a former textile mill in Mumbai, this exploration begins with the ingredient," Robb Report India wrote. The restaurant is headed by chef Varun Totlani and is known for a modern Indian tasting menu built on local, seasonal produce. Its No. 26 finish is a world-list debut, separate from its No. 15 position on Asia's 50 Best earlier this year.

Naar: a Himalayan table of 16 seats

Naar is a different proposition entirely: a 16-seat restaurant in the Himalayan foothills at Kasauli, led by chef Prateek Sadhu. Its name translates to "fire" in Kashmiri, and its cooking takes its cues from the mountains — local produce, traditional preservation and wood-fired cooking across six distinct Himalayan seasons, Robb Report India reported. Alongside its No. 49 ranking, Naar won the Sustainable Restaurant Award 2026, recognised for local ingredients, community engagement and low-impact practices, according to The Daily Jagran and Lifestyle Asia.

How the list is decided

The World's 50 Best Restaurants, established in 2002, is voted by an academy of over 1,000 independent food writers, critics, chefs and experts who must have dined at a restaurant within the previous 18 months to vote for it, The Daily Jagran reported. That makes a debut by a 16-seat room in a Himachal hill town — a destination diners must deliberately travel to — a different kind of result from a big-city flagship, and it is why both Indian entries are being read as a geography story as much as a cooking one: the centre of Indian fine dining, on this list at least, now runs from a Mumbai mill to the Himalayan foothills.
